definitions.explanation: Describes food or drink that tastes good. One of the most common and useful adjectives for expressing positive opinions about food. Used in everyday conversation.

examples.japanese: これは{美味|おい}しいですね。
{美味|おい}しいレストランを{知|し}っていますか。
examples.english: Do you know a good restaurant?
examples.notes: 美味しい here means 'good' for food

examples.japanese: お{母|かあ}さんの{魚|さかな}はとても{美味|おい}しいです。
{友達|ともだち}が{作|つく}った{料理|りょうり}がとても{美味|おい}しくて、びっくりしました。
examples.english: The food my friend made was so delicious that I was surprised.

examples.japanese: この{店|みせ}の{魚|さかな}は{新鮮|しんせん}で{美味|おい}しいです。{毎週|まいしゅう}{来|き}たくなるほど{気|き}に{入|い}っています。
examples.english: The fish at this restaurant is fresh and delicious. I like it so much that I want to come every week.

notes: The kanji {美味|おい}しい is sometimes used but the word is more commonly written in hiragana (おいしい). The opposite is {不味|まず}い (mazui, bad-tasting). In casual speech, うまい can also mean delicious, though it's more masculine/casual. Saying おいしい when eating is a polite way to compliment the cook.
